hypotheses.justification: CoordinateSemiconvexOn lambda C f is defined as ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, ... so it holds vacuously when C is empty. If r < 0 then Metric.closedBall (0 : Point n) r = ∅ (Metric.closedBall_eq_empty), so any lambda (e.g. 0) works. The theorem is therefore true without hr. Proof: by_cases h : 0 ≤ r; in the positive case use the existing proof unchanged; in the negative case take lambda = 0 and discharge the membership x ∈ closedBall 0 r by rewriting closedBall as ∅ (Metric.closedBall_eq_empty.mpr (not_le.mp h)). The hypothesis hconv is still needed, so only hr is unnecessary.
